text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
*TAP pilots threaten to disobey government order to fly normal hours. Cabinet meeting today may approve new regulations to extend flying hours.
*Government is willing to raise public employee wages more than inflation in 1998 against the advice of the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
*Construction sector capacity use rose in second quarter of 1997, according to the National Association of Public Works Companies.
*Government plans to boost incentives to investment in tourism by further 7.8 billion escudos from September.
*Prime Minister Antonio Guterres interrupts holiday to preside at cabinet meeting because of crisis at TAP-Air Portugal.
*Government set to approve today the sale of 49 percent of BRISA, the state motorway operator.
*Credit Lyonnais Portugal should leave Lisbon stock market due sale of its retail network to Caixa Galicia, chairman Bernard Chantrelle says in interview.
